configuration.persistence: The probe wrote the changed enabled/config and fixture auth values to the private file; the file remained distinct from applying manager state.
configuration.fileWatcher: not observed; no automatic file-triggered apply

failedReconfiguration.lossAttribution: disconnectServer removed the prior catalog before the failing connectServers attempt; the SDK fixture does not provide a last-good transaction or service-level rollback.

auth.challenge: A controlled local HTTP POST returned 401 with WWW-Authenticate; the first tool call surfaced MCPTransportError.
auth.recovery: The fixture explicitly called reconnectServer with manual=true and an MCPAuthChallenge; the installed MCPManager auth handler returned a changed config with a fake local bearer value; the replacement connection and following call succeeded.
auth.automaticOAuthRefresh: not exercised: no AuthStorage/managed OAuth credential was configured
auth.remoteIdPConsentRefreshScopesProviderAut: unresolved; local challenge is not remote OAuth evidence
auth.secretHandling: Fake authorization values existed only in the owned temporary config/server process and were omitted from output; no real token or credential was used.

automatic.interruption: Called close() on the connected installed HTTP transport; this invoked its manager onClose path without calling reconnectServer directly.

recovery.distinction: Automatic manager callback recovery and explicit manual reconnect were each invoked and observed separately. The HTTP transport was logically connected, but no server-side HTTP SSE GET stream was active at the interruption; an abrupt network-level outage was not simulated.

cleanup.probeLogs: The successful probe emitted only sanitized JSON summary and phase markers; stderr was empty. No raw request/response, prompt, user file, secret, real endpoint, model or user path appeared in successful probe output.
cleanup.installedPackageScratchDeviation: One uniquely named temporary resolution probe was written into installed coding-agent package source during diagnostics, then removed before the final probe and cleanup. It is absent now; task-24 retained artifact inputs were not edited. The package payload was not strictly read-only throughout diagnostics.

limits: One loopback-only configuration/transport prototype; the installed consumer and retained immutable task-24 artifacts were reused without rebuilding or revision drift.

The temporary .mcp.json was read by a fixture-supplied config loader. This demonstrates the installed manager's config application/recovery behavior, not the default discovery provider's path precedence or a native file watcher.
The schema mutation was applied with explicit MCPManager.refreshServerTools; no tools/list_changed notification was sent and no file watcher behavior is claimed.
The HTTP interruption exercised the installed transport close/onClose reconnection path, not a network-level socket outage; zero server-side HTTP SSE GET streams were active at the time.

Failure followed explicit disconnectServer, so observed catalog loss is not evidence that a transactional apply overwrote a prior valid catalog. The service-owned transaction/rollback contract remains unimplemented/unproved here.

The local auth challenge validates only explicit SDK auth-handler/reconnect plumbing. Remote OAuth, IdP interaction, stored credentials, refresh tokens, scopes, provider-specific authentication and platform variation remain unresolved.
No application/service implementation, M0/M1 acceptance, or gate-03 passage is claimed.
